Control or empowerment? Stability or agility? Automation or augmentation? Last year , we explored these tensions and the need to navigate the polarities at play. But in 2026, the pace of change is sharpening the edges of these questions. Organizations are no longer just trying to balance competing forces: They are standing at a tipping point.
In our 2026 Global Human Capital Trends survey, 7 in 10 business leaders say their primary competitive strategy over the next three years is to be fast and nimble—to quickly adapt to and capitalize on changing business, customer or market needs. Leaders also report that the two most important drivers of success are accelerating how people and resources are orchestrated to perform work and increasing their organization’s and workforce’s ability to adapt to change and speed.

The classic S curve of growth has long described how businesses and work evolve: gradual lift, rapid acceleration, and eventual plateau. Today, that curve is compressing. AI and workforce transformation are accelerating the climb and bringing the plateau sooner (figure 1). Organizations are pressed to leap to the next curve more quickly to remain competitive. Long cycles of planning and predictable execution may no longer hold in a world where markets, technologies, and worker and customer expectations shift in real time. Success may now depend more on sensing change, experimenting quickly, and adapting continuously.
Today, new data and workforce insights—ranging from organizational digital twins to real-time analytics—make it possible to see where an organization sits on the curve and actively steer how and when to jump to the next one.

Historically, organizations jumped the curve by adding new technology, a strategy that may no longer be enough. Organizations will likely need to make the leap differently.
Competitive advantage is now primarily less driven by technology differentiation and more by cultivating the human edge. Technology—especially something as increasingly ubiquitous as AI—is replicable. People aren’t. Humans create competitive differentiation through adaptivity, creativity, and judgement amid uncertainty and change. When it comes to AI, value is unlocked through a reimagination of work that brings the best of humans and machines together in concert.
Indeed, recent Deloitte research with 100 C-suite leaders reveals that most organizations (59%) are taking a tech-focused approach when it comes to AI. But those taking a tech-focused approach are 1.6x more likely to not realize returns on AI investments that exceed expectations compared to those that take a human-centric approach. 1

Top 5 takeaways from ASIC hearing into KPMG
By
Malavika Santhebennur
8 September 2026 • 6 minute read
From a review of over 550 misconduct complaints to NDA reassurances, here are the main revelations from ASIC’s hearing into KPMG and the other three big accounting firms.
The corporate regulator appeared before the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Corporations and Financial Services for the Oversight of ASIC, the Takeovers Panel, and the Corporations Legislation where it provided insight into its investigation and surveillance activities on alleged misconduct at KPMG , as well as EY, Deloitte, and PwC.
Accounting Times provides a summary of the major issues discussed at the hearing.
Over 550 internal complaints at the big four firms
ASIC reported that it is reviewing 551 internal complaints received by the big four accounting firms relating to alleged misconduct since commencing surveillance from 1 July 2023.
ASIC obtained these complaints as part of its ongoing surveillance of audit conduct complaints, including potential whistleblower complaints, received by each of the big four audit firms, ASIC chair Sarah Court told the committee .
Court elaborated that ASIC asked the accounting firms to provide information on whether they have received complaints relating to misconduct by registered company auditors, such as the “misuse or sharing of confidential information”.
ASIC used its compulsory information gathering powers to obtain that material, she added.
When asked by the committee why their surveillance commenced in the “arbitrary” July 2023 period, ASIC executive director, enforcement and compliance, Chris Savundra , said he suspected it was because it was a reasonable period to begin, adding that the information gathered could lead to formal investigations.
“In no way are we limited in going further back,” Savundra said.
“In one instance, in relation to one complaint, we’ve now asked for information going back to November 2022 because it was a subsequent complaint that referred to an earlier one. We will follow the trail of where those complaints lead us.”
ASIC was asked about how it would proceed with the complaints it has received, to which Court responded that it is compiling the information for the purposes of a surveillance report to outline the findings.
It will also scrutinise individual complaints to ascertain if ASIC has to undertake further investigations or enforcement action on any particular issue.
“At a very early stage, I don't want to suggest that there are 550 serious whistleblower issues. We don't know, and there's a lot of work for us clearly to be looking through those complaints, getting more information as we need it,” Court said.
Court also told the committee that ASIC has directly received 139 reports of alleged misconduct relating to the big four accounting firms since 1 July 2023, and this may include services outside of audit functions.
KPMG still claiming privilege over documents
Court told the parliamentary committee KPMG is still withholding documents despite the corporate regulator seeking them by issuing notices.

Chess Event Coverage
GM Magnus Carlsen flagged GM Viswanathan Anand in the opening match of day three of the 2026 Tech Mahindra Global Chess League , but it couldn't stop Alpine APL Pipers tasting its first defeat when GM Vidit Gujrathi also lost on time. Vidit and the team would storm back later, however, to beat FYERS American Gambits 15-3 and take the sole lead on nine points out of a possible 12.
Four teams trail by three points, while Triveni Continental Kings finally got on the scoreboard with wins for GMs Wei Yi , Aravindh Chithambaram , and Alexandra Kosteniuk in the last match of the day.
Day four starts on Tuesday, September 8, at 6 a.m. ET / 12:00 CEST / 3:30 p.m. IST.

Match 10: CheQ Mumba Masters 12-3 Ganges Grandmasters
Match 11: FYERS American Gambits 3-15 Alpine APL Pipers
Match 12: Triveni Continental Kings 11-6 PBG Alaskan Knights
Standings After Day 3
All teams have now played four matches, with Alpine APL Pipers the only team to win three. The top-two teams after each has played 10 matches will contest the final match for the title.
Image: Global Chess League.
Let's take a look at the day's action.
PBG Alaskan Knights 9-7 Alpine APL Pipers
The headline clash here was, of course, a repeat of the 2013 and 2014 world championship matches, with Anand taking on Carlsen. The game was tense, with the current world number-one pressing hard with the black pieces but, by his own admission, losing control in time trouble:
I felt like I was outplaying him a little bit in the middlegame. I was really happy with the position from the opening and then later on, and then again I was a little bit shaky with little time and I think for a period there he was defending very, very well, not making it any worse, but then I just obviously resigned myself to a draw and then I randomly glanced at his clock and saw that it was out, which is how it goes sometimes.
Carlsen was briefly winning on the board, but in the end it was Anand who lost on time, somewhat against the run of play, since it had been the Norwegian who got down to seconds while his Indian rival still had time to think.

Nino Batsiashvili turned things around to win the match. Photo: Global Chess League.

The problem for Black is Ne5+, then the threat of Nd7+, forking the king and bishop, if Black takes the f6-pawn. items.storedText: Noida International Airport (NIA) has partnered with Tech Mahindra (NSE: TECHM), a leading global provider of technology consulting and digital solutions to enterprises across industries, to establish and operate an integrated Network and Security Operations Centre (NOC-SOC) for the airport. Our partnership with Tech Mahindra is a critical step in building a robust, future-ready network and cyber security framework that supports safe, reliable, and seamless airport operations. Through the integrated Network and Security Operations Centre, we will deliver round-the-clock monitoring, proactive threat detection, and rapid incident response across the airport’s critical IT and digital platforms. By combining deep domain expertise in critical infrastructure operations with proven security and network capabilities, we aim to help NIA build a trusted, resilient, and agile technology backbone.”With cybersecurity at the core of the airport operations, Tech Mahindra will work with NIA to build a robust, process-oriented ecosystem ensuring that the airport is supported by a reliable, secure, and scalable technology operations framework from the inception.News LinkNoida International Airport (IATA code - DXN) connects the greater Delhi area and Western Uttar Pradesh with other cities in India and the world. NIA is committed to an ambitious net zero emissions goal supported by sustainable design and operations principles.Yamuna International Airport Private Limited (YIAPL) was established for the development, construction and operation of the greenfield project - the Noida International Airport. The company, a 100% subsidiary of Zurich Airport International AG, is responsible for the implementation of the public-private partnership project in close partnership with the Government of Uttar Pradesh and the Government of India. The concession period for Noida International Airport commenced on October 01, 2021, and will run for 40 years. items.title: Brazilian natural gas operator Eneva working with Accenture on cloud transformation
items.storedText: Brazilian natural gas operator Eneva is working with Accenture and Google Cloud on a major cloud-driven digital transformation program aimed at optimizing operations, better serving customers, and driving growth. Eneva is Brazil’s largest private natural gas operator, engaged in exploration, production, and power generation. The company operates 15 natural gas fields in the Parnaíba and Amazonas basins, holding the country’s largest concession area (over 63,000 km2). Its generation portfolio includes 6.8 GW of contracted capacity, with thermal power plants across multiple states and the Futura Solar Complex located in Bahia. As part of its strategy, Eneva is working on a transformation program will modernize its technology backbone and make its operations more efficient and flexible. A key part of this transformation is the adoption of Google Cloud, which at the same time is driving the shift to a data-driven enterprise. This project is supported by consultants from Accenture. The first results of this multi-year program are already being reaped. With enhanced data insights from exploration and production, Eneva is optimizing its asset management maintenance and scheduling, resulting in more reliable and better-performing equipment. This boosts employee productivity by enabling maintenance operators to complete tasks in half the time currently required, freeing them up to focus on higher-value work. Eneva is also leveraging Google Cloud’s optimization tools alongside Accenture’s industry knowledge to save staff time and resources through the integration of data from various corporate and operational systems. “We’re not only seeing potential in the combination of cloud, data and AI – we’re already experiencing its transformative power across our business,” said Alexandre Ferreira, Chief Information Officer at Eneva. “With Accenture’s deep industry expertise and the advanced capabilities of Google Cloud, we’ve formed the ideal collaboration to drive transformation across our business for years to come.” “This program will enable us to serve our energy customers in Brazil with greater precision, agility, and innovation.” Commenting on the project, Scott Alfieri, Google Business Group lead at Accenture, said: “By combining Accenture’s experience in cloud technology and energy transformation with the advanced data and AI capabilities of Google Cloud, we’re helping one of the largest energy companies in Brazil unlock new levels of operational efficiency and customer impact. Together, we’re not just imagining change – we’re delivering it.”

items.title: Cruising into the Future: Carnival Cruise Line Selects DXC Technology to Power Technology Infrastructure
items.storedText: ASHBURN, Va., June 23, 2025 — DXC Technology (NYSE: DXC), a leading Fortune 500 global technology services provider, and Carnival Cruise Line, the world's most popular cruise line, today announced a multi-year agreement to power the cruise line’s technology infrastructure. This partnership will support Carnival’s guest experience across its global fleet, as well as its portside and shoreside operations. DXC will deliver reliable and scalable IT services designed to enhance operational efficiency, improve employee productivity and help ensure a seamless, connected experience for millions of guests sailing annually with Carnival. “At Carnival, we’re committed to delivering memorable vacations for our guests, and technology plays a vital role in ensuring they have the best onboard experience,” said Sean Kenny, senior vice president and chief information officer at Carnival Cruise Line. “The DXC team demonstrates exceptional technical expertise, responsiveness and a clear commitment to delivering on our long-term vision. With them as our trusted partner, we’re investing in technology that strengthens the foundation of our operations to provide a great experience for our guests across our 29 ships globally and supporting our dedicated team members both shipboard and shoreside.” Through the partnership, DXC will manage Carnival’s core IT infrastructure across all operational environments including shipboard systems, shoreside offices and port facilities. Using an employee-centric delivery model, DXC will ensure that the tools and services provided are tailored to support both Carnival’s workforce needs and a consistent guest experience. Services will include workplace support, IT service management, infrastructure operations and security risk management — all delivered with enhanced cybersecurity, expert-level staffing, automation support and a scalable model across its operations. This approach is built to improve resilience and ensure operational consistency across the company’s global footprint. "This collaboration with Carnival Cruise Line represents a significant milestone for DXC as we continue to expand our footprint in the hospitality and travel sectors,” said Chris Drumgoole, President, Global Infrastructure Services at DXC Technology. "Our goal is clear — deliver complete operational confidence for our customers by minimizing technology disruptions. By managing their complex IT operations and providing modern solutions, we're proud to help Carnival do what they do best, ensuring every guest enjoys their cruise vacation.” With deep engineering skills, industry expertise and a track record of success, DXC is a trusted technology partner to leading travel and hospitality brands around the world. From powering seamless guest experiences to enabling resilient and secure global operations, DXC helps companies modernize core systems and infrastructure to meet evolving customer expectations. For more information, visit dxc.com/cloud-and-infrastructure. About DXC Technology DXC Technology (NYSE: DXC) helps global companies run their mission-critical systems and operations while modernizing IT, optimizing data architectures, and ensuring security and scalability across public, private and hybrid clouds. The world's largest companies and public sector organizations trust DXC to deploy services to drive new levels of performance, competitiveness, and customer experience across their IT estates. Learn more about how we deliver excellence for our customers and colleagues at DXC.com. About Carnival Cruise Line Carnival Cruise Line, part of Carnival Corporation & plc (NYSE/LSE: CCL; NYSE: CUK), is the first cruise line to sail over 100 million guests and is proud to be known as America's Cruise Line, for carrying more Americans and serving more U.S. homeports than any other. Since its founding in 1972, Carnival has continually revolutionized the cruise industry and popularized the cruise vacation as an affordable and fun travel option. Carnival operates from 13 U.S. and two Australian homeports, as well as seasonally from Europe and employs more than 50,000 team members representing 120 nationalities. items.title: Nvidia's Two-Million-GPU AWS Order Puts Hard Numbers Behind the Hype - AD HOC NEWS

Nvidia's Two-Million-GPU AWS Order Puts Hard Numbers Behind the Hype Illustration mit AI erstellt.
The gap between Nvidia's soaring revenue projections and the skepticism that has trailed its stock all summer narrowed considerably this week. Amazon Web Services has committed to installing two million additional Nvidia GPUs across its data centers in 2027 and 2028, a deal that gives the chipmaker something its critics have said it lacked: concrete, multi-year demand commitments from a financially muscular cloud operator.
The AWS order lands on top of an earlier pledge for more than a million units and arrives in a week when Nvidia's earnings already dominated market conversation. For a company whose growth narrative has increasingly been questioned as circular — Nvidia has poured roughly $50 billion into AI labs that subsequently buy its own chips — the hyperscaler deal offers a counterweight. It demonstrates that established, deep-pocketed cloud providers are willing to lock themselves into Nvidia's roadmap years in advance.
The Quarter That Keeps Raising the Bar
Nvidia's fiscal second quarter delivered revenue of $96.2 billion, up 106 percent year over year, with the data center segment alone climbing 117 percent to $89 billion. Management guided for current-quarter revenue of $108 billion, plus or minus 2 percent, and signaled roughly 70 percent growth for fiscal 2028 — a figure Morgan Stanley noted sits well above its own 52 percent estimate and the roughly 40 percent market consensus.
The customer base is shifting as fast as the growth rate. Established hyperscalers lifted their contribution 102 percent to $48.7 billion, but a newer class of buyers — AI-native clouds, industrial firms, sovereign projects and specialists like CoreWeave and Nebius — expanded even faster, adding 138 percent to reach $40.3 billion. That diversification spreads the concentration risk inherent in relying on a handful of tech giants for a supplier's future. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Nvidia?
The Price of Growth
This expansion carries a literal cost. Memory-chip shortages have pushed Nvidia to raise prices on its Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell AI servers by 15 to 17 percent for deliveries from 2027 onward. Memory now accounts for roughly a quarter of a rack's cost, according to industry estimates, while the GPU share has fallen from over 80 percent to about 50 percent. New memory fabrication capacity is not expected online until 2029 or 2030, and TSMC, Nvidia's key manufacturing partner, plans price increases of 10 to 15 percent across all process nodes.
Management has itself flagged memory constraints as the limiting factor on growth. The Vera Rubin processor, whose deliveries begin this autumn, is seen as the next catalyst — and if AWS's additional capacity runs on that architecture, it would further cement Nvidia's position as the preferred supplier for AI infrastructure.
A Financing Machine in Chipmaker's Clothing
The company's transformation into something beyond a semiconductor vendor has become impossible to ignore. CFO Colette Kress put the share of expected fiscal 2028 business coming from financed customers at about 25 percent. Nvidia is building financing platforms exceeding $500 billion with partners including Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR. It has also committed up to $105 billion in leasing pledges for OpenAI's Ohio campus, alongside a $1.5 billion investment in SB Energy.

U.S. Army taps FedEx Dataworks and Google Cloud to modernize military logistics network under flagship Strategic Capital Initiative
By Martin Chomsky (Defence Industry Europe)
United States
|
August 31, 2026
Photo: U.S. Army.
The U.S. Army is turning to a FedEx Dataworks-led team and Google’s secure cloud infrastructure to modernize its domestic non-tactical logistics network. The project will cover supply-chain processes, materiel management and facilities across the Army’s organic industrial base.
The collaboration is the latest project under the Army’s Strategic Capital Initiative, which links priority military infrastructure requirements with commercially investable business models. The service said the approach could accelerate modernization without waiting for traditional procurement cycles while improving value for the Army, industry and taxpayers.
“Logistics win wars,” Army Secretary Dan Driscoll said. “Through the Strategic Capital Initiative, we’re pairing the Army’s depots and demand with FedEx’s logistics expertise and Google’s secure cloud to build a supply chain that moves as fast as the fight demands.”
FedEx Dataworks will apply commercial logistics analytics to help the Army build a predictive network for managing equipment and transportation. The work will include inventory optimization, demand forecasting and analysis of delivery routes and transportation modes.
“FedEx operates the world’s largest shipping and logistics network, connecting highly critical and precision-dependent supply chains for customers,” FedEx Corp. Chief Executive Officer Raj Subramaniam said. “We are honored to bring our expertise to support the U.S. Army’s vital mission.”
“We are evaluating transportation routing and modes to cut delivery times across the Army, and transitioning from a dated supply system to a predictive, intelligent network to ensure the warfighter receives critical equipment at the time of need,” Deputy Undersecretary of the Army Dave Fitzgerald said. The project will also examine how physical logistics infrastructure can be modernized alongside the Army’s digital systems.
The data environment will be hosted within Google’s Department of Defense Impact Level 5-authorized commercial cloud. Google Cloud will connect FedEx capabilities with legacy Army data sources while maintaining the identity-management and encryption controls required to protect national defense information.
The Army said the introduction of automation and advanced technology would support its civilian and military workforce rather than replace it. “Integrating advanced technology will not replace our workforce; it will remove friction and increase speed and effectiveness,” Fitzgerald said.
“By upskilling our personnel to manage these advanced systems, we are empowering our Soldiers and dedicated civilian workforce to timely deliver the critical support our warfighters require in a safer and smarter way,” Fitzgerald added. The Army and the FedEx-led team will establish working groups to assess existing networks, processes and technologies, with a final implementation plan for U.S.-based sites expected by November 2026.

Serco has secured a five-year contract with the Ministry of Defence (MoD) to operate and maintain the Solid State Phased Array Radar (SSPAR) at RAF Fylingdales in North Yorkshire. (Image: Freelancer)
This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today,

A new defence contract will help protect the UK from missile threats and support space monitoring.
Serco has secured a five-year contract with the Ministry of Defence (MoD) to operate and maintain the Solid State Phased Array Radar (SSPAR) at RAF Fylingdales in North Yorkshire.
The contract includes an option for a further two-year extension.
Anthony Kirby, chief executive of Serco Group, said: "We are immensely proud of our dedicated team at RAF Fylingdales who are entrusted to seamlessly deliver this continuous service, helping to defend the nation and protect our skies."
SSPAR forms part of the UK and US governments’ Upgraded Early Warning Radar (UEWR) programme and is critical to missile detection and tracking.
The radar also plays a key role in monitoring objects in low Earth orbit.
Serco’s team provides 24/7 support throughout the year.
In 2025, the SSPAR completed more than 5.9 million tracks of satellites in low Earth orbit.
Mr Kirby said: "We have a long history over sixty years supporting the UK Space Command, US Space Force and the Royal Air Force at RAF Fylingdales, with our people at the heart of this critical infrastructure asset.
"Our success in securing this contract reflects the strength of our expertise and growing capabilities in defence and builds on our recent strong momentum."
Serco will be responsible for radar hardware and systems operation, maintenance, analytical support, and training.
As part of the contract, a new software tool developed by Serco will be deployed.
The Enhanced Spacetrack Processor (ESP) will analyse large volumes of track data to determine the position, orbit, and size of objects in low Earth orbit.
Developed in collaboration with the RAF and UK Space Command, ESP replaces the long-serving United Kingdom Spacetrack Processor (UKSP), which was in use for more than 30 years.
The contract will also create new training and employment opportunities.
Serco will offer multiple Level 3 apprenticeships for school or college leavers, as well as Level 5 and 6 apprenticeships for current employees.
The company has partnered with Teesside University and Redcar & Cleveland College to develop an RAF Fylingdales-specific apprenticeship scheme.
This programme will equip individuals with essential skills, recognised qualifications, and a pathway to long-term careers in the defence sector.

Delivering real-time insights and traceability through AI-powered monitoring
Enabling end-to-end visibility and one-click exception resolution for a leading cash management company

Overview
In the cash management and secure logistics industry, operational accuracy and traceability are critical. Every cash bag movement must be accounted for to minimize financial risk, ensure compliance and maintain customer trust. However, many organizations still rely on fragmented systems and manual processes that make tracking cash movements challenging and exception investigations time-consuming.
Our client, a leading global cash management and secure logistics company, faced this challenge as it sought to improve visibility across its cash handling operations. Cash bags were captured on surveillance cameras, but movements were not always consistently recorded within operational systems. As a result, exception investigations often required employees to manually review video footage for 30-45 minutes per case, creating operational inefficiencies and delaying resolution.
To address these challenges, the client collaborated with HCLTech. Together, we engineered an AI-powered cash bag tracking and monitoring system that combined computer vision, custom AI models and enterprise data integration to create a searchable, auditable digital trail for every cash bag movement.
The Challenge
The client's cash management operations depended on a combination of surveillance systems and enterprise applications that operated largely in isolation. While cameras captured cash bag movements, the information was not consistently linked with operational records, creating visibility gaps throughout the cash handling process.
When exceptions occurred, such as missing cash bags, delayed processing or operational discrepancies, investigation teams had to manually search through large volumes of video footage to identify relevant events. Each investigation could take between 30 and 45 minutes, reducing productivity and increasing operational costs.
The absence of a reliable digital audit trail also increased business risk. Without timestamped evidence linked to operational events, it was difficult to determine what had happened during an exception, respond quickly to inquiries or provide audit-ready documentation.
The organization needed a solution that could leverage its existing infrastructure while providing end-to-end visibility, automated tracking and near real-time operational insights without requiring significant additional investments.
The Solution
HCLTech partnered with the client to design and deploy a cash bag tracking and monitoring system powered by Computer Vision and AI . The solution transformed existing camera infrastructure into an intelligent operational monitoring platform capable of tracking cash bag movements end to end.
Key highlights
Developed custom AI models for cash bag detection, teller machine monitoring and workstation utilization tracking
Created a unified tracking system where every cash bag movement is timestamped, searchable and linked directly to video evidence
Integrated seamlessly with the client's existing Video Management System and enterprise ecosystem
Deployed on the client's existing two-GPU server infrastructure without impacting network bandwidth
Connected camera-generated intelligence with enterprise data platforms, including Snowflake
Delivered near-real-time operational visibility through Power BI dashboards and reporting
Enabled workstation-level monitoring and utilization analytics to improve operational efficiency
Established a centralized platform that combines video intelligence with enterprise operational data for enhanced decision-making
The Impact
The AI-powered cash bag tracking and monitoring system fundamentally changed how our client managed exceptions and operational visibility across its cash handling network.
Key highlights
50% reduction in effort required for research cases
75% reduction in effort required for claims cases
20–40% reduction in SLA penalty exposure
Reduced exception investigations from 30-45 minutes of manual review to one-click resolution
Created a complete digital audit trail with searchable video evidence for every tracked cash bag movement
As a trusted AI Engineering partner, HCLTech helped the client modernize cash operations, improve operational efficiency and establish a scalable foundation for intelligent, data-driven cash management.

items.storedText: Persistent Systems on Tuesday reported a strong financial performance for the second quarter of FY26, well above Street expectations with strong growth in revenue and profit. Revenue from operations grew about 24 per cent to Rs 3,580.7 crore, higher than market expectations. Operating profit or earnings before interest and tax increased (EBIT) 43.7 per cent to Rs 583.7 crore, translating into an operating margin of 16.3 per cent compared to the estimated 15.7 per cent. In dollar terms, revenue stood at USD 406.2 million, rising 4.2 per cent sequentially and 17.6 per cent YoY. “We are pleased to report our 22nd sequential quarter of revenue growth, up 4.2 per cent QoQ and 17.6 per cent YoY, with operating margin improving to 16.3 per cent. This integrated approach brings together enterprise readiness for AI transformation, engineering hyper-productivity and business hyper-productivity, enabling clients to scale innovation, modernize their core and achieve measurable impact faster,” added Kalra.Persistent reported a total contract value of USD 609.2 million and an annual contract value of USD 447.9 million for the quarter ended 30 September 2025, indicating strong client demand and sustained deal flow despite macroeconomic uncertainties.

items.title: Be human, get $100 million bonus: EY tells employees who use AI at work - India Today
items.storedText: One of the Big Four consulting firms, Ernst & Young, better known as EY, has decided to reward its employees with million-dollar bonuses for showing human skills. The company has announced that it will invest $100 million, around Rs 800 crore, to reward employees who demonstrate skills such as judgement, adaptability, leadership and collaboration– skills it says are human and not easily replaced by AI in an AI-led workplace.EY US announced the new rewards programme on August 31, saying it wants to recognise employees who are not only adopting new technology but are also using it to create meaningful results. The programme will also recognise employees who contribute to the firm's culture and provide good client service.EY's decision to reward employees for these so-called human skills comes at a time when AI is bringing a big shift to the workplace and rapidly changing how people work. Companies are increasingly using AI to handle routine tasks, analyse information and improve productivity. But EY says technology alone is not enough. The firm wants to recognise people who can combine these tools with skills such as business understanding, judgement and the ability to adapt.How will the bonus programme work?The $100 million rewards programme will have three categories. Each category will reward employees based on the kind of work they do and the impact they make.The first is “Everyday leadership”. It will reward employees who help their teams learn, try new things, work together and take the lead in their daily work.The second is “Transformation that drives measurable results”. Under this category, EY will reward employees whose work brings real change through new ideas, technology, business growth or other improvements.The third is “Game-changing impact for the enterprise”. This category has been made for employees or teams whose work has a big and lasting impact on EY.The company notes that this bonus programme is not just for senior employees. EY says professionals across the organisation will be able to recognise their colleagues for good work. According to The Wall Street Journal, employees can receive spot bonuses of up to $500, while individuals or teams behind bigger achievements can receive awards of up to $25,000.Why is EY giving these bonuses?EY says the idea is to build a “tech-led, human-powered” workforce. The company wants its employees to learn how to use AI, but it also wants them to develop skills such as good judgement, leadership, adaptability and teamwork, things that AI cannot easily replace.Dante D’Egidio, EY Americas CEO and US Managing Partner, said the move is about preparing employees for a workplace that is changing quickly. “The pace and complexity of change in our industry require confident leadership,” he said. “This significant investment reinforces our commitment to building the workforce of the future by recognising the skills and behaviours needed to lead our profession and serve our clients with excellence.”- EndsPublished By: Divya BhatiPublished On: Sep 1, 2026 13:43 ISTAlso Read | Pakistani journalist records demo of driverless car, crashes into police vanAlso Read | Meta removes Facebook, Instagram ads using explicit content to spread malware after Govt sounds alarmAlso Read | Thailand gets a new passport, it will give free AI access to everybody

Microsoft and United Arab Emirates-based technology holding company G42 are accelerating their strategic partnership with a 200-megawatt data center expansion in Abu Dhabi, aimed at strengthening sovereign artificial intelligence infrastructure.
Backed by a $1.5 billion (KES 193.5 billion) strategic investment, the collaboration bridges the Middle East and East Africa, embedding strict security protocols into localized cloud environments. The partnership sets a new global precedent for deploying advanced technology across emerging markets while adhering to stringent data sovereignty regulations.
Expanding the Sovereign Cloud
The 200-megawatt capacity increase will be delivered through Khazna Data Centers and is scheduled to come online before the end of 2026. This expansion provides dedicated infrastructure for public sector organizations and regulated industries to run Microsoft Azure services without compromising national data security.
Brad Smith, Vice Chair and President of Microsoft, emphasized that the collaboration combines world-class technological capabilities with rigorous standards for safe and responsible artificial intelligence development.
The East African Connection
Beyond the Arabian Peninsula, the Microsoft and G42 alliance directly impacts the African digital economy. The companies are executing a comprehensive $1 billion (KES 129 billion) digital ecosystem initiative in Kenya.
Geothermal Data Center: A state-of-the-art facility in Olkaria, Kenya, powered entirely by renewable geothermal energy.
Local Language Models: Development of artificial intelligence models trained specifically on East African languages.
Skills Development: Broad digital training programs aimed at upskilling the local workforce.
This African expansion establishes a critical innovation hub that connects the Nairobi tech ecosystem with global processing capabilities.
Geopolitical Alignment and Governance
The commercial agreement is secured by a binding Intergovernmental Assurance Agreement developed in consultation with both the United States and the United Arab Emirates governments. The framework ensures compliance with international trade laws and secures sensitive intellectual property against unauthorized access.
As nations race to secure computational supremacy, the alliance between Microsoft and G42 demonstrates how private enterprises are navigating complex geopolitical boundaries to deliver sovereign technological independence.

Completion strengthens STTGDC’s ability to scale AI-ready digital infrastructure, building on strong operating momentum while maintaining continuity of strategy, leadership and customer commitment
SINGAPORE – Media OutReach Newswire – 2 September 2026 – STTGDC today announced the completion of its acquisition by a KKR-led consortium comprising funds managed by global investment firm KKR and Singtel, and unveiled a refreshed global brand, marking the beginning of the company's next chapter as a global digital infrastructure platform.
The transaction strengthens STTGDC's ability to execute a strategy already in motion, with long-term capital, increased financial flexibility and the consortium's global infrastructure experience providing continued growth and momentum. Customers will continue to be served by the same leadership team, operating discipline and long-term commitment that have underpinned the company's growth for more than a decade.
Retaining the STTGDC name, the refreshed brand reflects the scale, capabilities and global platform the company has built over more than a decade. It is anchored in Built Ready , expressing STTGDC's focus on delivering the reliable, resilient and AI-ready infrastructure required by customers across Asia, the United Kingdom and Europe.
"Today marks the most important turning point in STTGDC's evolution since we founded the company more than 12 years ago," said Bruno Lopez, President and Group CEO of STTGDC . "The completion of this transaction signals the beginning of a new chapter for our company. We have spent over a decade building a global platform with the scale, capabilities and operating discipline needed to support the next generation of cloud and AI growth. With the KKR-Singtel consortium's investment, we have greater capacity to grow and execute at scale while remaining true to the values and customer commitment that have defined STTGDC from its inception. Our refreshed brand reflects both the company we have become and the responsibility we carry as digital infrastructure becomes increasingly critical to economies, businesses and communities. Built Ready is our commitment to delivering the critical infrastructure our customers need to grow with confidence, while building responsibly and sustaining the trust of governments, customers and communities."

items.title: Deloitte Bets Big on AI, Data and Managed Services After $2.55 Billion Revenue Year - Kalkine
items.storedText:
A return to growth, with Revenue of $2.55 billion for the year to June 2026, was the headline. The more consequential story sits underneath it: the firm reorganising itself around artificial intelligence, data and recurring services, in a deliberate move away from the discretionary project work that has proved so volatile through the downturn.

The chief executive has been explicit that the model is shifting. 'The way professional services firms grow and create value is changing,' she said, 'and so we are changing with it.' That sentence is fast becoming the organising principle of the firm's strategy.

AI as tool, not just talking point

The firm is not merely advising clients on artificial intelligence; it is rewiring its own operations around it. A generative-AI tool has been rolled out to more than 13,000 Australian staff, part of what the Leadership calls Investment 'in our own transformation as technology changes how our people work'.

The logic is twofold. Internally, automating routine analysis and drafting lets the firm deliver work with fewer billable hours, protecting margins that were squeezed hard during the two-year revenue slide. Externally, embedded AI is increasingly what clients expect to be baked into every engagement, from tax compliance to systems modernisation.

The threat AI poses to consulting itself

The strategy is also defensive. Industry commentators note that generative AI could automate a large share of routine consulting tasks within a few years — some estimates suggest as much as 30 per cent — hollowing out the junior-heavy, hours-billed model on which firms like this were built. Fees for some standardised services could fall sharply as automation spreads.

Rather than resist that shift, the firm appears to be leaning into it: using AI to standardise and industrialise work, then selling the output at scale. The bet is that a firm which automates first can undercut rivals and win volume, even if the price of any individual task falls.

Data and recurring revenue

Sitting alongside the AI push is a broader tilt toward recurring, technology-enabled services. The managed services arm — which runs processes and platforms for clients on an ongoing basis rather than delivering one-off advice — posted double-digit growth over the year. A target has been set of building managed services into a $1 billion Business by 2030.

Data platforms are central to that ambition. Managing a client's finance, risk or compliance operations profitably at scale requires standardised, automated, data-rich systems — precisely the capability AI investment is meant to deliver. The AI, data and managed-services strands are, in effect, three parts of a single strategy: turn expertise into repeatable, software-like services that generate predictable revenue.

A reshaped firm

The appeal of Recurring Revenue is obvious after two years in which project Demand evaporated and dragged the Top Line down around 8 per cent before this year's rebound. Contracted, multi-year services are far less exposed to the swings in corporate confidence that hammered audit and dealmaking. The risks are real, however: building AI-enabled managed services demands heavy upfront investment in platforms and training, and the firm will be competing not only with rivals but with AI-native challengers.

Happiest Minds Technologies announces merger with ITC Infotech valued at INR18,087 crores
By Business Desk 4 min read · Published on Sep 7, 2026 · 10:20 PM IST
-Advertisement-
In a significant development within the Indian technology sector, Happiest Minds Technologies Limited has announced a proposed merger with ITC Infotech, valuing the combined entity at approximately INR18,087 crores. This announcement was made during an Investor/Analyst Call held on September 1, 2026, which was followed by a regulatory filing with the National Stock Exchange.
According to the details disclosed, Happiest Minds shareholders will receive 25 shares of ITC Infotech for every 81 shares of Happiest Minds they currently hold. Post-merger, ITC Limited will command a 73.4% ownership stake in the new entity, with public shareholders, including Mr. Ashok Soota, holding the remaining 26.6%.
Mr. Ashok Soota, promoter of Happiest Minds, will sell 22.1% of his 44.2% holding in the company across two tranches for a total cash consideration of approximately INR1,330 crores. The first tranche is anticipated to follow the Competition Commission of India (CCI) approval in Q3 of this year, while the second will proceed once shareholder approval is received in Q1 of FY28.
This merger is seen as a step forward for Happiest Minds in achieving its vision to become a USD1 billion revenue company, a target now set for FY28 instead of FY31. Happiest Minds' Co-Chairman and CEO, Mr. Joseph Anantharaju, highlighted that the merger strategically positions the company to expand its client base and capabilities in digital, AI, cloud, and other technology domains, aligning with industry trends.
The valuation and swap ratios were based on assessments by independent valuers, PwC and Grant Thornton, and reviewed by ICICI Securities. Happiest Minds was valued at 15.1 times its FY26 EBITDA, and ITC Infotech at 13.6 times. The merger is expected to conclude within the next 15 months, with a listing of the merged entity's shares on Indian bourses to follow in Q2/Q3 of FY28.
The merger will see the combined entity serving over 800 clients worldwide, leveraging complementary strengths in various technology sectors. Both companies will continue to operate independently until regulatory approvals are secured.
